parsed.why: No trans-specific offence, but documented police rape/beating of trans people with impunity, heavy stigma, and weak accountability; offset partially by a sanctuary community and embedded third-gender traditions.

Cross-dressing legal, courts convicting attackers of trans tourists and a police officer for beating a trans woman; hostility is political/rhetorical with detention gaps, but rule of law works for trans people.

Enforced criminalisation (five-year minimum, no maximum), 93% social hostility, religious calls for killing, no LGBTQ organisations or recourse; thin trans data extrapolates from these structural signals.

Criminal statute documented as used to arrest trans people on gender expression, police genital checks and public filming, outing campaigns, religious authority opposing transition, no recognition or anti-discrimination law.

National trans-rights statute, self-ID, hate-crime coverage, choice of prison placement, attackers prosecuted, 96/100 freedom rating; enforcement uneven and resident violence prevalence high, but visitor-facing machinery is protective.
